overview: This paper proposes OPRIDE, an offline preference-based reinforcement learning algorithm that enhances query efficiency via an In-Dataset Exploration (IDE) strategy for selecting informative trajectory pairs and a Variance-based Discount Scheduling (VDS) mechanism to mitigate reward overoptimization during policy extraction.

modules.name: Offline Dataset Processing and Segment Sampling
modules.description: Handles the loading of offline datasets (e.g., D4RL, Meta-World), trajectory segmentation into fixed-length fragments, and management of reward-free and preference-labeled data buffers for subsequent query selection and training.

modules.name: Ensemble Reward Model Architecture
modules.description: Implements the multi-head reward network architecture using a shared backbone with distinct output heads, supporting the computation of ensemble reward estimates and Bradley-Terry pairwise preference probabilities.

modules.name: Ensemble Value Function Architecture
modules.description: Implements the multi-head Q-function and Value-function networks based on Implicit Q-Learning (IQL), designed to process distinct rewards from the reward ensemble and output multiple value estimations for uncertainty quantification.

modules.name: In-Dataset Exploration (IDE) Query Selection
modules.description: Realizes the core query selection logic by calculating the maximum difference of value differences across the trained ensemble value functions for trajectory pairs within the offline dataset, identifying the most informative queries to minimize value uncertainty.

modules.name: Preference-Based Reward Learning
modules.description: Implements the reward model training loop using the cross-entropy loss on the accumulated preference dataset, and the subsequent annotation of the reward-free offline dataset using the aggregated ensemble reward predictions.

modules.name: Variance-Based Discount Scheduling (VDS)
modules.description: Implements the dynamic discount factor adjustment mechanism by computing the variance across the ensemble Q-value estimates, identifying high-variance state-action pairs based on a top percentage threshold, and assigning a smaller discount factor to these points to enforce pessimism.

modules.name: Offline Policy Extraction with Dynamic Discounting
modules.description: Implements the IQL-based policy extraction step, incorporating the variance-based dynamic discount factors into the Bellman target calculation to train the final policy while mitigating reward overestimation in uncertain regions.

modules.name: OPRIDE Main Training Orchestrator
modules.description: Controls the overall two-phase iterative workflow, managing the alternating sequence of reward ensemble training, value ensemble training, IDE query selection, preference annotation, and final policy extraction within the allocated query budget.

modules.name: Evaluation and Benchmark Runner
modules.description: Evaluates the learned policies across locomotion, manipulation, and navigation tasks, computing normalized episode returns and standard deviations to compare against baseline offline PbRL methods.

modules.name: Query Efficiency and Ablation Study Suite
modules.description: Provides experimental configurations for ablation studies comparing IDE against disagreement-based and random query selection, evaluating VDS against standard discounting or reward penalization, and measuring performance scaling across varying numbers of preference queries.

modules.name: Experiment Configuration and Logging Infrastructure
modules.description: Manages hyperparameter configurations (e.g., ensemble size, discount factors, variance thresholds), random seeding for reproducibility, and integration with experiment tracking tools for logging training metrics and evaluation results.
